subject: Clarify invoice line-itemization for mini-buckets & rounding policy
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@novamed.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: acct-billing@novamed.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice question: apparent rounding and mini-buckets

Hi Markus,

Hope you're well — we've just reviewed the October invoice and there's a line I can't reconcile. The attached PDF (Invoice_20261031.pdf) shows several small "mini-bucket" line items that look like minimums applied to very short sessions. Example: multiple calls with ~12 tokens of output were billed as the full 100-token minimum and then rounded up again. That doubled the expected charge for a handful of bursts.

Can you explain how the mini-bucketization is being applied and the rounding behavior? Specifically: (1) is there a 100-token floor per request regardless of prefix reuse, (2) how does KV/prefix reuse reduce (or not) the billed unit, and (3) what rounding rules produce what looks like double-rounding on the invoice line?

Attached: Invoice_20261031.pdf and usage-breakdown.csv (sample of a few sessions).

We have a renewal conversation next quarter and need to understand if the current packaging will systematically overcharge for our intermittent micro-calls. If there's a reconciliation path, please advise.

Thanks,
Elena
Billing Operations
NovaMed
[Attachment: Invoice_20261031.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: usage-breakdown.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novamed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice question: apparent rounding and mini-buckets

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for the examples in the CSV, that helps a lot. Short answer: what you're seeing is the interaction of (A) per-request atomic minimums (the "mini-bucket" floor), (B) our context-coalescing heuristic, and (C) invoice line aggregation that currently applies per-call rounding after floor application. I'll explain below and propose next steps.

1) Floor / mini-bucket: for the package your account is on the system enforces a per-call minimum of 100 tokens when a call does not hit the prefix/KV cache threshold for reuse. That minimum is applied before any per-model token rounding. In practice, repeated short calls that don't reference the same cached prefix can each trigger the floor.

2) KV/prefix reuse: when requests reference an active prefix or the existing KV cache within the same conversation window, the runtime will credit repeated tokens and avoid recharging the full floor; however, there is a window (default ~10m of inactivity) where the prefix is considered stale and the floor can reapply. Your CSV shows many calls spaced ~12–15 minutes apart, which is long enough to fall out of the reuse window.

3) Rounding and invoice line aggregation: after the floor is applied per-call we round to the billing quantum (in your case 50-token quantum for certain SKUs). Because the floor is applied first, a 12-token call -> 100-token floor -> then rounded to the nearest 50 results in 100 (no change), but if there is an upstream aggregation step that groups microcalls into a single invoice line incorrectly, it can look like an extra rounding step. We recently rolled a change to invoice line smoothing that reduced noisy lines, but it wasn't enabled on your tenant due to a packaging mismatch (older invoice schema).

Proposed immediate actions:
- I'll open a reconciliation ticket and flag a provisional credit for the 8 most impacted microcalls (based on your CSV).
- Kimberly (cc'd) will validate the credit and coordinate the billing adjustment run.
- Sergio, can you review whether NovaMed's invoice schema is pinned to the legacy line-aggregation path? If so, we should migrate to the "coalesced invoice" pipeline which aggregates the microcalls into a single amortized line and prevents double-rounding.

If you want, we can also temporarily lower the mini-bucket floor on a pilot to see how it affects unit economics for you (useful for renewal talks). I'll attach a proposed reconciliation workbook and a short explainer we can share with procurement.

Let me know if that plan sounds good and if you'd like a quick 20-min sync next week to walk through the examples.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-reconciliation.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]
